Issue #772

The Briefing For Engineering Leaders

November 27th, 2026

Friday 27th November issue is presented by Shopify

Agents Are Shopping This BFCM. Build For Them.

Shoppers now find and buy across agents, apps, and storefronts. With Shopify’s Fall ’26 Edition, every Liquid and Hydrogen storefront and checkout is agent-ready by default.

WebMCP tools hand browser agents structured data so they stop scanning screenshots and faking clicks.

And shop.dev connects any agent or app to Shopify Catalog, cart, checkout, and Shop Pay. One connection, no key.

Explore The Fall ’26 Edition

Why High Achievers Always Have Impostor Syndrome

— Steve Huynh

tl;dr: “When I get to know someone at work on a deeper level, they will usually confide to me that they feel like an impostor. I’d put it at around 90% of the time, so that’s pretty much all of us, and it’s not really a secret. I’ve always wondered why. Could it be that we’re all pretending to be professionals, one step away from being discovered, while the people who would uncover our secret are busy disguising their own incompetence?”

Management Career Wellbeing

Take Your Curiosity Seriously

— Sharif Shameem

tl;dr: What am I trying to get at here? What point am I actually trying to make? I think it’s this: (1) Your curiosity is important. (2) You should indulge your curiosity by working on projects that have no clear payoff. (3) A life where you frequently indulge your curiosity is a remarkably more interesting life than one where you don’t. (4) Your subconscious is intelligent in a way your conscious mind is not, and your curiosity is the mechanism by which you are drawn to important ideas you cannot logically understand.

  Career

Agents Are Shopping This BFCM. Build For Them.

tl;dr: Shoppers now find and buy across agents, apps, and storefronts. With Shopify’s Fall ’26 Edition, every Liquid and Hydrogen storefront and checkout is agent-ready by default. WebMCP tools hand browser agents structured data so they stop scanning screenshots and faking clicks. And shop.dev connects any agent or app to Shopify Catalog, cart, checkout, and Shop Pay. One connection, no key.

Promoted by Shopify

API AI Agents

You Don’t Get Paid For What You Did, But For What You’re Going To Do

— Kent Beck

tl;dr: I always have a twinge of entitlement when I see it. I created some value in the world. Some of that value should come back to me, no? That kind of thinking — create value → get paid —violates a fundamental economic principle that I’ve been noodling on, a principle that I haven’t seen anywhere else (← so likely it’s wrong, but still worth thinking about). Here’s the principle: you don’t get paid for what you’ve done, you get paid for what you’re going to do.

Management Career

“Everything should be made as simple as possible. But to do that you have to master complexity.”

— Butler Lampson

Tech Predictions For 2027 And Beyond

— Werner Vogels

tl;dr: “Yes, I am a techno optimist. I honestly believe that technology can play an incredibly positive role in our lives. But that doesn’t mean that I don’t see the dark side. Technology could just as easily be used for malicious acts and we need to put equal energy into dealing with bad actors and an unpredictable geopolitical landscape. As such, some of my predictions are a bit of a reality check, focused on things you should be thinking about right now. Others challenge you to imagine what’s possible in the decade to come.”

  Leadership IndustryTrends

A Simple View On Progressive Software Architecture

tl;dr: The way software is built is changing. Yet, architecture thinking is more important than ever. Learn about key principles and frameworks we believe are critical to thriving in this new, chaotic world.

Promoted by IcePanel

IndustryTrends Architecture

The Explorer Pattern For Product Invention And Development

— Will Larson

tl;dr: “The Explorer Pattern is one individual or team building a functional implementation that minimizes cross-team and cross-functional impacts as much as humanly possible, and then reconciling the details with other teams after that prototype is completed, accepting that this approach can require very substantial rework to that initial development.”

Leadership Strategy Product

I’m A 100x Engineer Now

— David Veszelovszki

tl;dr: “After 30+ years of coding the old-fashioned way, I’m extremely enthusiastic and about 100x faster with AI! It has changed my entire workflow, and my life. While I’m writing this, I’m painting the kids’ room. Claude helped select the type and color of the paint, calculate the amount of paint I needed, and look up where to buy it. I made all the decisions, I own everything that happened, while Claude did the research and prepared the decisions for me. That’s also exactly how I work.”

Product DevEx AI

How To Be More Ambitious: A Tutorial For Humans With Models

— Felix Rieseberg

tl;dr: “I frequently proclaim (together with other people working on AI) that we ought to be more ambitious when using it. It’s become a rallying cry. Whenever we see something impressive, we repost and write “we’re not ambitious enough”. I understand how tricky it is to follow that advice, so here’s a tutorial on being more ambitious. I think of ambition in four types: Speed, Altitude, Depth, and Range.”

Guide Productivity AI

Null Pointer

Debugging Biz

Issue #771

The Briefing For Engineering Leaders

November 24th, 2026

Tuesday 24th November issue is presented by Unblocked

Reclaim The Time You Spend Steering Agents

Your agents can read the code, but not why it was written that way.

Unblocked gives them that history from your PRs, tickets, and Slack, so you spend less time correcting them.

“With Claude Code and Unblocked, I fire off a query, minimize the tab for half an hour, and come back to working code." - Matt Thompson, Staff Engineer at Codat

Try For Free Today

How to Set And Protect Your Boundaries At Work

— Yue Zhao

tl;dr: “Many of us know in theory that setting and protecting boundaries is important. However, we tend to forget to do it, particularly in high-pressure, highly competitive, or “we’re going to change the world” environments. Here are three reasons I see most often in my clients for a lack of boundaries.”

Career Wellbeing

How Can I Spot The Early Signs That A Change Is Going Off Track?

— Andi Roberts

tl;dr: “Notice unexpected behaviours, repeated exceptions, workarounds, changes in relationships and shifts in what people discuss or prioritise. Look for places where the change is working better than expected too. Explore what these observations might mean before deciding whether, and how, to intervene.”

  Leadership ChangeManagement

A Pile Of MCP Connectors Is Not A Context Engine

— Dennis Pilarinos

tl;dr: You rolled out Claude Code and Cursor, wired up MCPs to GitHub, Jira, and Slack, and built shared repos of skills. Your agents still open PRs that miss how your team builds, like a pattern you retired last year or a decision buried in Slack. Each MCP adds a source, but nothing tells the agent which one is current. Read how to pull the right context for each task and settle conflicts before the agent writes a line.

Promoted by Unblocked

Architecture AI Agents

How Do You Become Known As A Good Engineer?

— Leila Clark

tl;dr: “In today’s job market, it can feel hard for people to stand out. But as someone who also receives hundreds of resumes a month, all accompanied by the same AI-generated emails, I can also tell you that it’s harder than ever to find candidates who seem to be trying at all.”

Staff+ Career

“Creativity is seeing what others see and thinking what no one else ever thought."

– Albert Einstein

Shipping 100+ PRs To Production In A Week

— Will Larson

tl;dr: “Many people in the industry are shipping far more PRs than I am, but I think it’s interesting to discuss how I got here specifically, especially in the context of a fintech company shipping software that’s critical from reliability, security, and revenue perspectives. We’re also six years old, so we were not built from zero to be an AI-native company, but have instead had to retrofit our approach at each step along the way.”

  CodeReview DevEx AI

Are Architects Surrendering Their Thinking To AI?

tl;dr: "We're just a meat bucket in the middle, moving information from left to right". Jacob Shadbolt (CEO/Co-founder of IcePanel) explains why AI can draft your diagrams but can’t tell you why the system was built that way, and why (human) collaboration is still key.

Promoted by IcePanel

Leadership Architecture AI

Deterministic Simulation Testing

— Unmesh Joshi

tl;dr: Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic and the same fault can produce different execution traces on different runs. Deterministic simulation testing addresses this by replacing real clocks, networks, and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop. This allows simulating both hard failures and routine slowdowns — such as network and disk latency spikes—and more importantly makes every execution reproducible. 

DeepDive Testing DistributedSystems

The Ultimate List Of Best Software Architecture Books (2027)

— Patrick Roos

tl;dr: “In this blog post, I present you a list of the best software architecture books you should read in 2027, and what interesting software architecture books will be published in 2027.”

Books Architecture

10 Lessons For Agentic Coding

— Drew Breunig

tl;dr: “I’ve been keeping a running list of tips for agentic coding: guidelines or rules one might give to someone just getting started with Codex, Claude Code, Pi, or any other agent. Ideally each tip is generalizable guidance, relevant to any agentic programming. I’m also looking for durable lessons that will stick around as models and harnesses improve.”

AI Agents

In our team’s retro this week that hit me pretty hard, and it was a real learning moment for me. The Rule Of No Surprises

— Ben Balter

tl;dr: “If something would surprise someone when they find out later, tell them now, not once it’s convenient or fixed. Lead with the headline, say what you need, name the rule, and do it consistently enough that people stop checking your work. If you manage people, thank them for early warnings, or you’ll get watermelon status updates: green on the outside, red on the inside.”

Leadership Communication

"The quality of a leader is reflected in the standards they set for themselves."

— Ray Kroc

Design For Understandability

— Jonathan Schuster

tl;dr: “Just as our industry has learned to design software for testability, we can also design it for understandability. We can use ideas like design by contract, class invariants, modularity, and more to create systems that we can understand one piece at a time, rather than piling more onto the big ball of mud and hoping it doesn’t all collapse.”

  CodeQuality Architecture

Why Are Agentic Workloads Different From Traditional Applications?

— Paddy Srinivasan

tl;dr: Agentic work needs effective infrastructure: security hardened code execution, persistent sessions, fast startup, and governed tool access. Checkpointing and forking let that work branch, pause, and continue across devices and teammates. Active CPU billing ties costs to actual consumption. DigitalOcean Managed Agents lets developers focus on user value instead of infrastructure management.

Promoted by DigitalOcean

Infrastructure Agents AI

Self-Reinforcing Quality / Adopting Verification Pattern

— Will Larson

tl;dr: The verification pattern itself is more similar to the chain-of-thought pattern, which aims to steer the harness towards your desired outcome in a clear way. For example, we require that each pull request generate a verifications/{pr_num}.md file that describes each step the harness took to verify the changes, and also what it was unable to verify.

CodeQuality CodeReview AI

No AI Slop: A Manifesto

tl;dr: “The world moves especially fast these days, but the goal of these resolutions is to embrace our important human role in harnessing AI safely, responsibly, in a way that creates value for everyone, and that will be relevant for years to come.”

Leadership Ethics AI

Shell Tricks That Actually Make Life Easier (And Save Your Sanity)

— Christian Hofstede-Kuhn

tl;dr: “Here are some tricks that aren’t exactly secret, but aren’t always taught either. To keep the peace in our extended Unix family, I’ve split these into two camps: the universal tricks that work on almost any POSIX-ish shell, and the quality-of-life additions specific to interactive shells like Bash or Zsh.”

Issue #769

The Briefing For Engineering Leaders

November 17th, 2026

Tuesday 17th November issue is presented by WorkOS

You Can’t Leak A Token You Never Held

Card numbers live in a vault, not in the app that charges them.

Agent credentials should too. A token in an agent’s runtime spreads into context, logs, and error payloads, and a leaked one works anywhere until it expires.

WorkOS Relay keeps OAuth tokens out of the agent and attaches them on the way out, only to allowlisted hosts.

See How Relay Works →

One-Way And Two-Way Doors

— James Stanier

tl;dr: “Having your team be able to distinguish between one-way doors and two-way doors can dramatically increase the velocity of your team and also prevent them from making mistakes. This language was popularised by Jeff Bezos, and it can explain why some teams are able to move so quickly without breaking the things that matter, whilst other, more bureaucratic teams grind to a halt waiting for several layers of sign-off.”

Leadership DecisionMaking

How AI Will Change Engineering Leadership In 2027

— Bjorn Roche

tl;dr: “As 2027 approaches, I’m thinking about what AI will be like next year, how it will impact my job and what I’ve learned about it so far. I think 2026 was the year where we started to glimpse how powerful it can be, and 2027 will be the year when we will refine our intuition and learn when and how to apply AI most effectively. Here are some thoughts on what I’ve learned and what I think is next.”

  Leadership AI IndustryTrends

You Can’t Leak A Token You Never Held

tl;dr: Card numbers live in a vault, not in the app that charges them. Agent credentials should too. A token in an agent’s runtime spreads into context, logs, and error payloads, and a leaked one works anywhere until it expires. WorkOS Relay keeps OAuth tokens out of the agent and attaches them on the way out, only to allowlisted hosts. 

Promoted by WorkOS

Auth Agents Security

How Can I Recover From Sustained Stress And Avoid Exhaustion?

— Andi Roberts

tl;dr: “Recovery from sustained executive stress depends on regular, deliberate rest that matches the load you are carrying. Protect sleep first, then build short breaks, personal time and longer periods of restoration into how you work.”

Career Wellbeing

“I have not failed, but found 1000 ways to not make a light bulb.”

— Thomas Edison

Asking Better Questions

— Michael Heap

tl;dr: “There's nothing more terrifying than getting a "Hey, quick question. Are we on track to launch by X?". It's not the question itself that's terrifying. It's everything you don't know when you hear it.”

  Leadership Communication

The AI Operating Layer: A Stable Foundation For Changing Industry Rules

tl;dr: AI agents and tools can now make everyone a coder. That’s a good thing… until it’s not. As AI adoption grows, so does risk exposure. The AI Operating Layer whitepaper from Coder explains the 5 requirements every environment needs to contain risk safely.

Promoted by Coder

— Thomas Wolf

tl;dr: “We're entering a strange new era where software is never finished, source code is no longer secret, and every user becomes the architect of their own digital world.”

AI IndustryTrends

How I Use AI (Oct 2026)

— Ben Stolovitz

tl;dr: “I still believe I use AI fairly typically, but I’ve had a notable change in background. Last October, I was an engineer on Microsoft’s Windows AI team. I am now a research engineer at Salesforce AI Research. I spend more time supporting scientists & building rapid prototypes, rather than working with a large team of engineers. I spend about ~$3,000/​month in tokens.”

Productivity AI Career

The Watchmaker: Building A Mechanical Watch In A Database

— Trevor Dwyer

tl;dr: “By the end, a database had designed a 26 mm watch movement of 34 parts, checked that no two parts share space, worked out by itself how to take it apart, and run it for a minute. Every tick was computed in SQL.”

Entertaining SQL Database

It’s worth noting that most of my work nowadays is on my boxing app, which is a fairly small codebase where I’m the only one merging code in… so if you’re at a large company, it probably won’t translate very well.”

New Units Of Knowledge

— Kevin Kelly

tl;dr: “In the past, books were the primary unit of knowledge. When computers came along, knowledge was combined with action, and the shareable unit became software code. The web made the page and the link the unit, and for twenty years knowledge spread hyperlink by hyperlink. Code itself became shareable as packages and libraries that anyone could snap together. Later, mobile phones refined the knowledge unit into the “app.” Tremendous amounts of potential knowledge and action are compressed into a tiny app, which can be shared, bought, and sold.”

Issue #767

The Briefing For Engineering Leaders

November 10th, 2026

Tuesday 10th November issue is presented by Unblocked

Reclaim The Time You Spend Steering Agents

Your agents can read the code, but not why it was written that way.

Unblocked gives them that history from your PRs, tickets, and Slack, so you spend less time correcting them.

“With Claude Code and Unblocked, I fire off a query, minimize the tab for half an hour, and come back to working code." - Matt Thompson, Staff Engineer at Codat.

Try For Free Today

Designing An Engineering Strategy

— Aleix Morgadas

tl;dr: “The kernel of a strategy contains three elements: a diagnosis, a guiding policy, and coherent action. This definition resonates with me, maybe because now I’m not lost on strategy expectations. Now that we know what Strategy is, we need to adapt this to Engineering Strategy.”

Leadership Strategy

Five Studies Changing How I Think About AI In Software Engineering

— Brian Houck

tl;dr: “Each paper tackles a different question. Some measure the productivity impact of AI coding assistants. Others examine how those gains propagate through the software delivery process, explore what developers actually want from future AI systems, or reconsider the kinds of debt we should be paying attention to in an AI-assisted world. Despite coming from different research groups and using very different methodologies, they all seem to be converging on the same underlying story.”

  Management AI

How Much Of Your Week Is Spent Answering Questions?

tl;dr: Everyone does their homework first. But when sources conflict, pinging an engineer becomes the shortcut. Unblocked weighs the evidence from your code, pull requests, tickets, production data, and discussions, so your agents and teammates alike find the answers on their own. You step into threads only for real engineering problems, and your agents get to working code without you babysitting.

Promoted by Unblocked

Management Tools+Setup

The Revised Rules Of Engineering Management With Will Larson

— Will Larson, Gergely Orosz

tl;dr: Two hour interview with Gergely. Areas more focussed for engineering leaders are: (1) What does a CTO do (35:11). (2) How engineering management has evolved. (42:48) (3) Revised rules of engineering leadership (1:16:25) (4) How to become a CTO? (1:25:57).

Podcast Leadership Management

"Believe you can and you're halfway there.”

— Theodore Roosevelt

Writing As A Thinking Tool

— Murat Demirbas

tl;dr: “Writing is also the reason I remember anything. I refer back to my own blog constantly. Because I strained my brain writing those posts, rereading them re-fires the same neurons, and I reconstruct the understanding quickly. In this sense, the blog became my external memory. The thoughts I never wrote down do not stick well, because they were never fully thought.” Murat shares his rules for writing.”

  Career Learning Writing

See How Your Team’s AI Coding Workflows Compare

tl;dr: 68% of surveyed engineering leaders report a wider performance gap between engineers since adopting AI. Only 19% say they turn effective AI practices into team or company standards. Span’s Coding Agents in Practice: Q4 2026 brings together perspectives from over 100 engineering leaders on agent adoption, code review, and sharing what works. Compare your team’s approach with peers and identify where to focus next.

Promoted by Span

item.title: Issue #765
item.content:encoded:
Issue #765

The Briefing For Engineering Leaders

November 3rd, 2026

Friday 30th October issue is presented by Atono

Your Agent Passed Every Test. So Why Was It Still Wrong?

A coding agent built a working API endpoint in two hours. The code looked right. Every test passed.

Except the endpoint returned deleted users that weren't supposed to be there. The agent had made an assumption nobody asked it to make, then written tests that treated that assumption as correct.

For Lex Vorona, Atono co-founder and senior software developer, it's a familiar problem: agents can make perfectly reasonable decisions that are completely wrong for your product.

Lex shares what he's learned from working with coding agents, including:

  • Why passing tests doesn't always mean an agent built the right thing

  • How he decides when to supervise agents and when to let them work independently

  • Why visibility into an agent's decisions matters as autonomy increases

  • What he's learned about giving agents the context they need to succeed

Read The Story

Becoming A Better Writer

— Gergely Orosz

tl;dr: “Writing is an increasingly important skill for engineering leaders. Poor writing can hamper career progression, above a certain level. Tactics for more clear, more frequent and more confident writing.”

Leadership Career Writing

How To Sequence Annual Planning And Reorgs

— Yue Zhao

tl;dr: “A planning team is formed for each important area of investment for the next year. Each team has a planning lead and includes critical members from each function that needs to be involved in the planning (e.g., marketing, sales, customer support, operations, finance, engineering, design). This team meets according to the planning cycle, coming together for brainstorming sessions, prioritization, resource planning, and executive reviews.”

  Leadership CareerDesign

Your Agent Knows Your Code. But Does It Know Your Product?

tl;dr: Better prompts won't solve every agent problem. Your agent might understand the codebase but still miss the product decisions behind it. We break down three ways to give Cursor and Claude Code the context they need: repo-level instructions, connected documentation, and context tied directly to the work, including where each approach falls short.

Promoted by Atono

Guide AI Agents

Fast And Slow Ways To Improve Your Reputation

— Sean Goedecke

tl;dr: “To get a good reputation in tech companies, you need to work on important projects. However, you need a good reputation first in order to get assigned important projects. Doesn’t that make it impossible to get started?”

Career

"Write a short story a week. It's not possible to write 52 bad short stories in a row."

– Ray Bradbury

Hunger Beats Tenure: Advice For Junior Engineers

— Felix Rieseberg

tl;dr: “This month, I laid the traditional coding interview to rest. As a hiring manager at Anthropic, I stopped asking candidates to do them. It had a good run: Being able to quickly define problems and find elegant solutions was a weak but useful predictor for how successful you’d be on my teams.”

  Management Hiring Career

Every Model. Privacy With Proof.

tl;dr: TrustedRouter gives you hundreds of AI models through one open source, OpenAI-compatible API. Find the right model at the right price, with automatic provider fallback to keep your app running. TrustedRouter’s attested gateway never logs your prompts or outputs, and you can verify its attestation yourself. Already using OpenRouter? Change your base URL and API key. Try it today with free credits at TrustedRouter.

Promoted by TrustedRouter

Security API AI

Self-Reinforcing Quality / Adopting Verification Pattern

— Will Larson

tl;dr: “You can argue that your harness was already performing these steps, but it’s actually hard to say whether it was or wasn’t. My sense is that it often wasn’t happening: I’ve seen too many pull requests go to CICD that had failed basic lints that could have been run locally to believe the harness was always running them. Now the harness has to explicitly document that it’s done those steps, or acknowledge it hasn’t. This allows the harness to self-drive more effectively.”

DevEx CodeQuality

How DoorDash Reduced LLM Search Costs By 98% Without Losing Accuracy

tl;dr: “Reasoning models and evidence retrieval evolve at different speeds. Separating them lets us improve either independently and choose the balance of quality, freshness, latency, and cost that each workload needs. For DoorDash’s QIU workload, that separation preserved accuracy while substantially lowering search costs. The broader engineering lesson is to make grounding an explicit interface that teams can evaluate and change as their requirements evolve.”

CaseStudy CostOptimization AI

The Skill Of Using AI Agents Well

tl;dr: “What tips, tricks, approaches are you using to improve your efficiency when using agent harnesses? I personally focus on Claude Code & Codex CLI mostly for single person software development, but I welcome suggestions for other tools and other areas of use. Ideally you share what you tried and what works for you and I try it myself and see whether it improves my workflow. Here are my discoveries (with level of confidence).”

We use “large codebase” to refer to a wide range of deployments: monorepos with millions of lines, legacy systems built over decades, dozens of microservices across separate repositories, or any combination of the above.“

tl;dr: “Applications that read their own signals, decide what to change, ship the change, and check whether it worked. And once software can improve itself, it can improve the machinery that improves it: better observability, sharper detection, deeper investigations, better fixes, each loop tightening the next one.”

Try For Free Today

Seven Phrases I Stole From Staff Engineers

— Louise Deason

tl;dr: “I have spent the last several years collecting these phrases the way other people collect house plants. I steal them. I write them down. I try them out in my own meetings, badly at first, and then with increasing precision until they start to work. Below are seven I now use constantly, with the underlying move each one is actually doing - because the phrase is the surface; the move is the thing.”

Leadership Communication Staff+

When You Disagree With A Decision

— Michael Heap

tl;dr: “By pairing strong commitment with deep empathy, you respect both the decision-making process and the people executing it. Own the direction, do the work as if you were solely responsible for its success, and keep your eyes open for the genuine friction that proves it’s time to talk again.”

[Webinar] How To Stop Babysitting Your Agents

— Brandon Waselnuk

tl;dr: You write the rules files, maintain the skills, and paste in the Slack thread your agent missed. But hand-curated context goes stale, and when the sources disagree, your agent can’t tell which is right. Join us live on Oct 28 (FREE) to see how a context engine helps agents get it right the first time.

Promoted by Unblocked

Events AI Agents

The Arrival Trap

— Mike Fisher

tl;dr: “The arrival trap costs the most in abandoned compounding. Somewhere right now, a 33-year-old with a decade of hard-won judgment is deciding the window has closed, while the data says they are still twelve years younger than the average founder of a top-performing company. Somewhere a team is killing a sound strategy in year two because someone sold it as a year-one story. The trap pushes a few people to fake success. It pushes far more to quit real success in progress because it’s arriving on an unfashionable schedule.”

Leadership Strategy Career

"Teach for the future; you have to live in it"

tl;dr: “How do you review code at the volume agents produce it? On the Claude Code team, once we had high coverage and deep reviews, we started optimizing for the minimum amount of human review time that doesn't raise reverts or incidents.”

tl;dr: Ask an AI agent to add versioning to file uploads, and it might rewrite parts of your upload system that didn't need changing. Catching that is now the engineer's job. Here are the five things we look for in senior engineers in the age of AI.

tl;dr: “I’ve heard some say that AGI will make us more efficient at work. And that it really won’t have much of an impact on our personal lives. I find this belief to be common in people who lack creativity and cannot envision a future beyond automating knowledge work.
